title: Scared of speaking English?
reason: 本集从昨日的职场分歧沟通轮换到英语学习与主动输出，主题正面回应“理解强、开口调用弱”的瓶颈。内容说明即使语言水平不错，害怕犯错和被评价仍会阻碍真实交流；所选表达简单、高频，可直接迁移到英语会议、技术交流和日常对话中。

targetExpressions.meaning: to feel afraid or worried about doing something
targetExpressions.usage: Many learners are scared of speaking because they do not want to sound wrong.

targetExpressions.meaning: to do or say something incorrectly
targetExpressions.usage: It is normal to make mistakes while learning a new language.

targetExpressions.meaning: despite the fact that; used to introduce a contrast
targetExpressions.usage: She joined the discussion even though she felt nervous.

targetExpressions.meaning: to be skilled or successful at an activity
targetExpressions.usage: You can be good at reading English and still need more speaking practice.

targetExpressions.meaning: to understand a person or situation because of a similar experience
targetExpressions.usage: Many professionals can relate to feeling nervous in their first English meeting.

targetExpressions.meaning: to have a relationship with or be caused partly by something
targetExpressions.usage: Speaking anxiety can be connected to how learners see themselves.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the phrase from the episode: Beth was ______ speaking Spanish because she did not want to make mistakes.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Beth says she is scared to speak because she does not want to make mistakes.
The transcript stresses that mistakes are normal and can help language learners learn.

options.text: Learners sometimes make mistakes when they speak.
Learners sometimes do mistakes when they speak.
Learners sometimes create mistakes when they speak.
Learners sometimes build mistakes when they speak.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the contrast: Hanan felt nervous ordering coffee ______ her English assessment results were very good.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: “Even though” introduces the contrast between her strong English level and her nervousness in a real conversation.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence best matches Hanan's experience?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Hanan was fluent and had good assessment results, but real conversations still felt difficult.

options.text: She was good at English but found some everyday conversations difficult.
She could not read or understand any English.
She was only nervous because her assessment result was poor.
She found ordering coffee easier than the assessment.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Georgie's reaction: “I'm sure that's a situation lots of people can ______.”
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript uses “relate to” for understanding a situation because something similar has happened to you.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the explanation: Speaking anxiety can be ______ the beliefs learners have about themselves.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme says experts think speaking anxiety is connected to beliefs about ourselves.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: According to the episode, why can irrational beliefs increase speaking anxiety?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Learners may believe others will judge their mistakes negatively, even when that belief is not based on fact or logic.

options.text: They can make learners expect negative judgement.
They give learners a larger vocabulary.
They come only from the people around the learner.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: According to the programme, how many words does a typical English speaker use in daily conversation?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The answer to the programme's factual quiz is between 20,000 and 30,000 words.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80-120 words. Use this structure: (1) topic—why speaking a foreign language can feel stressful; (2) Hanan's experience and two causes of anxiety; (3) the programme's conclusion about speaking and mistakes. Phrase bank: “even though”, “make mistakes”, “be connected to”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate English is enough; rare vocabulary and complex sentences are not required.
referencePoints: Pippa and Beth both describe feeling nervous when speaking another language.
Hanan's English assessment was strong and she was fluent, but ordering coffee still made her nervous.
Many learners can relate to speaking anxiety even when their language ability is good.
Experts connect severe anxiety with irrational beliefs, low self-perception and fear of negative evaluation.
Learners may feel less confident because they cannot show what they are really like in a new language.
The programme says mistakes are normal, learners need to try speaking, and mistakes can help them learn.
